subject: Pilot ops: who does what — deployment checklist and next steps

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Pilot ops: who does what — deployment checklist and next steps

Hi Alicia / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed ops checklist so we can start aligning owners and lock a tentative start date. Goal is a 30-day pilot starting first week of September, with a 2-week smoke/canary before full evaluation.

Summary of agreed success criteria
- Latency: average p95 generation < 450ms for 1k token prompts on your core workflows
- Cost: target unit cost <= $0.004 per token (post-batching/quantization adjustments)
- Quality: automated eval hits >= 90% on the sample prompt set we reviewed
- Security: no egress of PII outside customer VPC (for private deployment) or encrypted in-transit + at-rest if hosted

High-level evaluation plan and milestones
1) Week 0 (pre-onboard): exchange minimal infra contacts + procurement PO window (you)
2) Week 1–2: staging/canary (small traffic, smoke tests) — validate connectivity, auth, sample prompts
3) Week 3–6: full pilot (real traffic, metrics collection, cost/latency tracking)
4) Week 7: wrap-up and go/no-go decision with regression report

Owner / responsibility checkpoints (draft)
- Cloud infra & firewall rules: CloudFleet DevOps (Responsible)
- App integration (API calls, SDKs): CloudFleet Product/Platform team (Accountable)
- Security & evidence for SOC2 checklist: CloudFleet Security (Consulted) + Redwood Security (Evelyn Hart) (Informed/Support)
- Procurement / legal: CloudFleet Procurement (Responsible for PO)
- Redwood: deployment support, model serving, observability, runbooks (Responsible/Support)

Can you confirm the CloudFleet technical contact for infra (name + email), procurement PO timing, and whether you prefer Redwood Hosted or Redwood Private (VPC) for this pilot? I attached a short deployment checklist and data access matrix for your team to review.

Attachments: [Attachment: pilot-deployment-checklist.xlsx (12KB)], [Attachment: data-access-matrix.pdf (9KB)]

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm infra contact and procurement window by EOD Wed 8/18
- Redwood SE (Karthik) to send minimal staging steps and firewall rules
- Kickoff call wk of 8/24 to align engineers and schedule the canary

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Confirming:
- Technical contact for infra is Samir Patel (samir.patel@cloudfleet.com) — he'll own firewall/VPN and have DevOps ownership on the staging project.
- Procurement: we can cut a PO within 10 business days once we have the scope doc; Procurement in CC (procurement@cloudfleet.com) — they expect line-item pricing and term length.

2) For the SOC2 evidence you mentioned — can Redwood share the specific logs/fields you capture so we can match with our audit checklist?

I synced with Samir and Procurement — we can target a Sept 1 canary start if Redwood can deliver staging steps and a short runbook by 8/24.

Hi Alicia / Samir — quick tech follow-up from our SE side with ownership clarifications and the minimal staging steps.

Short answers to Alicia's Qs:
1) Hosted dedicated instance: yes — we can reserve a dedicated replica pool for the canary. It will be a dedicated allocation with soft isolation; we will provide expected SLOs in the staging runbook.
2) SOC2 evidence: Evelyn, copying you — I've attached the fields we typically surface (request_id, timestamp, request_headers, model_id, token_counts, latency_ms, route_id). If Private deployment is used we can additionally provide VPC flow logs and host-level logs under the customer's KMS keys.

Minimal staging checklist (what we need from CloudFleet)
- Allowlist Redwood IPs (I will send exact list) or establish an IPsec tunnel
- Provide a staging API key (scoped to staging) or configure OIDC trust with our test client
- Share a 20–30 prompt sample set and expected metrics baseline (CSV)
- Short window for smoke traffic: 6–12 hours to validate correctness and latency

Suggested canary cadence
- Day 1–2: smoke + latency profiling (low volume)
- Day 3–14: ramp to 5–10 TPS for core flows, collect cost/latency/quality metrics

- Informed (I): Redwood CS (Ben Carter) + Redwood AE (Kimberly Park) — pilot progress and executive summaries

Procurement asks (Procurement in CC):
